The answer is yes, in fact, it was already spreading. But this attack, which Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky called "an exemplary operation" will inevitably raise the stakes another notch. Russia, which is currently engaged in a non-stop campaign to batter Ukraine's civilian population into submission with daily missile and drone strikes , has called it "a dangerous escalation". It follows the suspected Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian dry-cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland at the weekend, which the Kremlin described as an act of terrorism. Ukraine's long-range drones have also previously struck Russia's Baltic oil terminal at Ust-Luga. Some of Ukraine's more audacious long-range drone attacks – what Zelensky likes to call "long-range sanctions" – have also struck targets thousands of kilometres beyond Ukraine's borders with Russia, deep inside Siberia. The most notable of these was last year's Operation Spider's Web, which involved a specially adapted lorry that drove close to a Russian strategic nuclear bomber airbase and released a "swarm" of explosive drones that damaged or destroyed several expensive bombers. And Ukraine has also been active further south in Africa where its forces have targeted Russian mercenaries from the Africa Corps, the successor to the infamous Wagner Group that was accused of carrying out numerous human rights abuses. clusters.text: Nepal’s PM Balendra Shah is in New Delhi for a two-day visit – his first since coming to power in March. India will provide Nepal with a $1.62bn economic package in the wake of August’s devastating floods in the country, which led to the deaths and disappearances of thousands of people. The sum announced on Monday is one of its largest-ever relief commitments, and comes as New Delhi boosts ties with its Himalayan neighbour, where it competes with China for influence. The announcement followed talks between India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah, who is in New Delhi for a two-day visit – his first bilateral trip abroad since coming to power in March. “We express our deep condolences for the loss of lives caused by the devastating floods in Nepal in August,” Modi said, standing alongside Shah in New Delhi. “To support Nepal’s reconstruction, and give fresh momentum to its long-term development, we announce a development cooperation package worth 240 billion Nepali rupees [$1.6bn].” August’s floods, which scientists say were caused by the effects of climate change, were triggered when part of a mountain glacier collapsed and a torrent of water and mud flooded down into Nepal’s Rasuwa and Nuwakot regions, as well as into China’s Tibet region on August 26. More than 1,300 people have been confirmed dead, and more than 5,000 remain missing. In October, the United Nations’ climate loss and damage fund set aside a sum of $20m for aid to Nepal. India’s package will include a $377m grant for post-disaster reconstruction and new infrastructure projects, and a $1.24bn line of credit for energy projects, the countries said in a joint statement. India is Nepal’s largest trading partner, accounting for more than 60 percent of its imports, worth $8.6bn, while China accounts for 13 percent, or $1.8bn, according to World Bank figures. Besides the flood relief package, the pair agreed on further cooperation in education and research, satellite communications, and sustainable urban development. The two leaders also jointly opened a train link connecting the countries. “May the friendship between Nepal and India be one where trust stands as tall as the Himalayas,” said Shah.

Islamabad, Pakistan – Pakistan is poised to send an astronaut into space for the first time on Wednesday, when an air force pilot joins China’s Shenzhou-24 mission to the country’s Tiangong space station. Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, 40, will fly as a payload specialist alongside commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer Wu Yi. The spacecraft is scheduled to launch from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China at 8:18am Beijing time (00:18 GMT), or 5:18am in Pakistan. Speaking at a news conference in Jiuquan on Tuesday, China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) spokesperson Zhang Jingbo said the mission would mark the first joint flight by Chinese and foreign astronauts in the country’s crewed space programme. After reaching orbit, the spacecraft will carry out a rapid, autonomous rendezvous lasting about three and a half hours before docking with the forward port of the station’s Tianhe core module, Zhang said. Ali’s stay will be brief. He will return to Earth on board the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft after a short joint flight, while Zhu Yangzhu, a member of that crew, remains in orbit for a year, Zhang said. Pakistan’s Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (SUPARCO) has said Ali will spend about a week on the station. “I want to assure you that I am not flying for myself. I carry the name of Pakistan on my shoulder, the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis,” Ali told reporters during the crew’s conversation with the media. Ali and Khurram Daud, a second Pakistani selected for astronaut training, are Pakistan Air Force pilots. They were selected through a three-stage process that began with screening in Pakistan and included medical, psychological and technical assessments. CMSA named them reserve astronauts on April 22 earlier this year. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met them in Islamabad the following day, and on April 24, China’s Space Day, they joined the Astronaut Center of China in Beijing for training. clusters.text: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has proposed preventive safeguards against fraudulent electronic banking transactions, including customer-set transaction limits, the facility to disable digital payment channels, and an additional layer of authentication through a trusted person mechanism (TPM). The measures are aimed at giving customers greater control over how and to what extent digital payment channels are used. The draft follows public feedback on the RBI’s discussion paper issued on April 9. The regulator had then sought views on measures such as payment delays for certain high-value transfers, trusted-person checks for vulnerable customers, and limits on credits to certain accounts. The November draft, however, does not include the proposed one-hour payment delay or an annual credit ceiling under which credits would be held in shadow mode. The RBI has invited comments on the draft by December 14. Under the draft, banks must allow customers to disable one or more digital payment channels linked to their accounts and subsequently re-enable them through physical or digital interfaces. Once a channel is disabled, customer-initiated debit transactions through it would not be permitted until it is re-enabled. Customers would also be able to set or modify limits on the maximum amount per transaction, per beneficiary, and for aggregate transactions during a day through a particular channel. They could set an overall daily limit across all digital payment channels, as well as specify a time window during which selected channels would remain disabled. Banks may offer additional controls beyond those specified in the draft. For cards, banks must provide customers with the facility to switch domestic and international transactions on or off and set or modify transaction limits across point-of-sale (PoS) terminals, automated teller machines (ATMs), online and contactless payments. These provisions would not apply to gift and transit prepaid payment instrument (PPI) cards. The draft also proposes a “stop switch” facility to immediately disable all future outward debits from a customer’s account. Once activated, customers would not be able to initiate debit transactions, create new payment mandates or standing instructions, or register their accounts on new third-party Unified Payments Interface (UPI) applications. clusters.text: Anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship. On Monday, the newly public AI company announced the launch of Claude Ship , a suite of AI agents for automating code reviews, fixes, and approvals of routine code changes. The latter is the more interesting part of this new set of tools, as AI coding tools already offered code review features before now. 30 street lights stolen in Dhurwa, RMC lodges police plaint
clusters.text: Ranchi: Around 30 street lights have been stolen from ward 40 in Dhurwa, prompting Ranchi Municipal Corporation (RMC) to lodge a case diary with the Dhurwa police. The civic body warned miscreants of strict legal action against those involved in theft or damage of civic assets.“Municipal property is meant for the convenience of citizens and development of the city. Theft or damage of government property and attempts to disrupt public amenities are serious offences,” RMC said in a statement.The matter came to light after the Ward 40 councillor on Monday informed additional municipal commissioner Sanjay Kumar about repeated theft of street lights in the area. Acting on Kumar’s directions, an assistant engineer of the electrical wing conducted an inspection and lodged a complaint at Dhurwa police station.RMC also appealed to residents to help protect public property and report instances of theft, vandalism or suspicious activities involving streetlights, civic equipment and other municipal assets. Residents can report such incidents to the corporation on its toll-free number, 18005701235.

clusters.title: Months before boards, Class XI admission process starts in city
clusters.text: Ranchi: City-based CBSE and ICSE schools have announced subject-wise cut-offs, entrance tests, and scholarships for Class X students interested in registering themselves in their preferred institutes and stream.While ICSE Class 10 board exams is scheduled to run from Feb 15 to March 31, 2027, CBSE exams will be held from Feb 16 to March 9.DAV Nirja Sahay has opened provisional registration based on Class X half-yearly and pre-boards. Its stream-wise criteria vary for existing students and outsiders, with PCM requiring 55% and 60%, respectively, in English, mathematics, and science.“The school also offers tuition fee waivers, ranging from 25% for students scoring 85-89% to a full waiver for those above 97%. Sports medal winners are eligible for concessions of up to 50%, while girls receive relaxation in cut-offs,” principal Kiran Yadav said.Sarala Birla Public School stressed on academic commitment, discipline, and participation in co-curricular activities. “Students scoring above 90% in board examinations, state toppers, Olympiad rank holders, RMO qualifiers and national-level sports medal winners are eligible for a 50% concession on admission fees,” principal Manisha Sharma said.ICSE-affiliated Metas Adventist School has started provisional registrations, based on merit or entrance exam scores, said principal Sunil Kumar.Bishop Westcott Boys’ School, Namkum, will make application forms available from next week. It admits both boys and girls to Classes XI and XII. Oxford Public School will begin issuing Class XI application forms next week, said academic administrator Ravi Shekhar, while DAV Public School, Hehal, has invited applications for the upcoming session.JVM Shyamali has opened its application window, with an admission test scheduled for Jan 17. The school has prescribed eligibility criteria for streams and limited direct-admission merit seats, while its existing students are exempt from the aptitude test, subject to eligibility.Loyola Convent School is offering application forms in both online and offline modes. “Students joining from other schools are expected to trust the institution’s learning process, follow academic norms and attend classes regularly,” principal Paramita Saha said..Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news.
